accepted.question_text: Find a direct proof that βη-strong reduction is confluent, without relying on a prior confluence proof for λβη-reduction. Equivalently, give a self-contained confluence proof for the combinatory theory of βη-strong reduction that is independent of λ-calculus.

evidence.quote: Statement. Is there a direct proof of the confluence of βη-strong reduction? The βη-strong reduction is the combinatory analogue of βη-reduction in λ-calculus. It is confluent. Its only known confluence-proof is very easy, but it depends on the having already proved the confluence of λβη-reduction. Thus the theory of combinators is not self-contained at present. Is there a confluence proof independent of λ-calculus?

accepted.question_text: Decide whether ticket entailment is decidable. In equivalent combinatory terms, determine whether there is an algorithm that, for any type τ built from variables with the arrow constructor, decides whether τ is inhabited in the restricted combinatory logic based on the basis B, B′, I, W.

evidence.quote: Statement. Is ticket entailment decidable? The question is whether there is a decision-algorithm for the implicational fragment T→ of the propositional logic called ticket entailment. Equivalently, is there one for the simple type-theory of the restricted combinatory logic based on B, B′, I, W? Is there an algorithm that, when applied to any type τ, will decide whether there exists a term X in this system such that X : τ is provable?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the range property holds for the least lambda theory H that equates all unsolvable terms: for every combinator F, either H proves F M = F N for all closed M and N, or there are infinitely many closed terms M_i such that no two terms F M_i are identified by H.

evidence.quote: Statement. Does the range property hold for the theory H? Consider the least lambda theory H which equates all unsolvable terms. Take any combinator F. Prove that either H ⊢ F M = F N, for all closed M, N, or there are infinitely many closed Mi, such that no two of terms F Mi are equated under H.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether some applicative combination built only from the combinators B and ω is a fixed-point combinator. Here ω satisfies ωx ⇒ xx and B satisfies Bxyz ⇒ x(yz); the question is whether there exists a term Y over {B, ω} such that Yx = x(Yx), or at least is a fixed-point combinator in that sense.
accepted.context_brief: fixed-point combinator from B and ω

evidence.quote: Statement. A fixed point combinator from B and ω alone? The combinator ω satisfies the reduction rule ωx ⇒ xx and the combinator B is as usual Bxyz ⇒ x(yz). Is there an applicative combination of B and ω which is a fixed point combinator?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exist lambda terms that are typable in the extension of simply typed lambda-calculus with positive recursive types μp τ, using the introduction and elimination rules for μp τ when p occurs only positively in τ, but are not typable in Fω.

evidence.quote: Statement. Are there terms untypable in Fω but typable with help of positive recursive types? Consider an extension of simply typed lambda-calculus obtained by adding the construct µp τ for types τ containing only positive occurrences of p. Are there terms typable in this system that cannnot be typed in Fω?

accepted.question_text: Decide whether a given finite set of proper combinators is combinatorially complete. A satisfactory solution would provide an abstraction algorithm parameterized by the chosen finite basis of proper combinators and would report failure on non-bases.
accepted.context_brief: basis decision problem for proper combinators

evidence.quote: Statement. Basis Decision Problem. The basis decision problem, originally stated in [Statman, 1993], is to decide whether a given finite set of proper combinators is combinatorially complete. A good solution would be an abstraction algorithm, parameterized by a given set of combinators, which returned an error message on non-bases.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the word problem is decidable for the system consisting of all proper combinators of order less than 3. Here the word problem asks whether two applicative combinations of members of the system are βη-equal.

evidence.quote: Statement. Word problem for combinators of orders less than 3.

The word problem for a set of combinators C is to determine if two applicative combinations of members of C are βη-equal. We ask if the word problem for all proper combinators of orders less than 3 is decidable.

accepted.question_text: Identify which one-step effective strategy results known for combinatory logic remain valid for lambda-calculus, including the existence of effective one-step cofinal, Church-Rosser, and enumeration strategies, and the nonexistence of an effective confluence function.

evidence.quote: Statement. Which results on one-step effective strategies carry over from combinatory logic to lambda-calculus? The following results on reduction and conversion strategies in combinatory logic are surveyed in [Statman, 1997]: • There is an effective one-step cofinal reduction strategy. • There is an effective one-step Church-Rosser strategy. • There is an effective one-step enumeration strategy. • There is no effective confluence function.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every weakly normalizing pure type system is also strongly normalizing. More specifically, resolve the Barendregt-Geuvers-Klop conjecture beyond the known non-dependent cases and establish whether weak normalization implies strong normalization for arbitrary pure type systems.
accepted.context_brief: weak versus strong normalization for PTSs

evidence.quote: Statement. Is every weakly normalizing PTS also strongly normalizing? The conjecture that the above statement can be answered in the positive is known as the Barendregt-Geuvers-Klop conjecture.
It is natural to wonder how the result can be extended to larger classes of pure type systems.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether uniform universal generators exist in combinatory logic with weak reduction or in lambda-calculus with β- or βη-reduction. A term M is a uniform universal generator if there is a non-trivial context C[*] such that M reduces to C[N] for every closed term N.

evidence.quote: Statement. Do uniform universal generators exist? A term M is a uniform universal generator iff there is a non-trivial context C[∗] such that M ↠ C[N] for each closed term N. The above question was first stated in [Statman, 1993], and it is open for either CL (with weak reduction) or lambda-calculus (with β- or βη-reduction).

accepted.question_text: Characterize which finite sets E of equations between intersection types preserve normalization when intersection type assignment is extended by the conversion rule that allows replacing a type τ by any σ with τ =_E σ. In particular, determine conditions ensuring strong normalization for such systems.
accepted.context_brief: normalization under equations on intersection types

evidence.quote: Statement. Which equations on intersection types preserve normalization? Let E be a finite set of equations between intersection types, and let =E be the congruence generated by E. Extend intersection type assignment by the rule: Γ ⊢ M : τ / Γ ⊢ M : σ (τ =E σ). Under what condition such a type assignment system has the (strong) normalization property?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the typability hierarchy of Fω collapses at level F1; that is, whether every pure lambda-term typable in Fω is already typable in F1, where Fn is the subsystem allowing constructors of order n.

evidence.quote: Statement. Does the typability hierarchy of Fω collapse on F1? The type assignment system Fω can be split into an infinite hierarchy of subsystems Fn. It is conjectured [Urzyczyn, 1997] that every pure lambda-term typable in Fω is typable already in F1.

accepted.question_text: Resolve the inhabitation problem for the remaining open intersection type systems listed in the source—specifically HL, HR, Sc, CDZ, and DHM—and more generally determine decidability boundaries for inhabitation in intersection type systems, including variants with recursive intersection types.

evidence.quote: Statement. Inhabitation for intersection type systems. The inhabitation problem is to determine whether there exists a closed term of a given type.
The question remains open for the systems HL, HR, Sc, CDZ, DHM. Yet another open question is the inhabitation problems for systems with recursive intersection types, cf. Problem 11.

accepted.question_text: For each integer n ≥ 2, characterize exactly the lambda terms typable in the stratified polymorphic type assignment system of order n, where the elimination rule for ∀ is restricted by the level of the quantified variable.

evidence.quote: Statement. For every n, determine the set of terms which can be typed in the stratified polymorphic type assignment system of order n.

It turns out that ⊢0 has the same typing power of the Curry type assignment system, and ⊢1 assigns types to all and only the normal forms. Find a characterization of the set of terms typable in the system indexed by n, for n ≥ 2.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether, in simply typed lambda-calculus extended with finite products and finite sums, the equational theory =βη is the maximum consistent typically-ambiguous congruence containing =β. Equivalently, determine whether every proper typically-ambiguous extension of =βη is inconsistent.
accepted.context_brief: maximality of βη with finite sums

evidence.quote: Statement. Is the equational theory of typed λ-calculus with finite sums the maximum consistent typically-ambiguous congruence?

The main question is: Is =βη maximum amongst consistent typically-ambiguous congruence relations containing =β? A (possibly) weaker version of the question is simply: is it the case that the only typically-ambiguous congruence relation properly extending =βη is the inconsistent relation?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the subtype entailment problem is decidable for simple subtyping constraints over non-structurally ordered trees. Concretely, given a finite set of inequalities C = {τ_i ≤ τ′_i} and terms τ, τ′, decide whether C entails τ ≤ τ′.

evidence.quote: Statement. Is the subtype entailment problem decidable? We ask if the entailment problem with simple subtyping constraints over non-structurally ordered trees is decidable.
For a finite set of constraints C = {τi ≤ τ′i}i=1...n of constraints and terms τ and τ′, we consider the entailment C |= τ ≤ τ′.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether recursive types in the sense of Mendler can be defined in system F. Existing results show that β-conversion alone is insufficient, so the open question is whether the polymorphic βη-lambda-calculus can define those recursive types.

evidence.quote: Statement. Can recursive types be defined in system F? It was shown by Geuvers and Spaławski that inductive types in the style of [Mendler, 1991] are definable in the polymorphic βη-lambda-calculus. It is however an open question whether recursive types as in [Mendler, 1987] are also definable.

accepted.question_text: Find tree representations of lambda terms whose equality exactly matches the contextual equivalences determined by the sets W of weak head normal forms, T of top normal forms, SA of strongly active terms, SA_X of strongly active terms depending on X, and HA of head active terms.

evidence.quote: Statement. Find trees representing contextual equivalences

The question is to find tree representations of λ-terms whose equalities coincide with the following contextual equivalences: 1. ∼W where W is the set of weak head normal forms, 2. ∼T, where T is the set of top normal forms, 3. ∼SA, where SA is the set of strongly active terms, 4. ∼SAX, where X is a set of λ-terms and SAX is the set of strongly active terms depending on X, 5. ∼HA, where HA is the set of head active terms.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every easy term is also simple easy. Here a closed term E is easy if, for every closed term M, the theory λβ + {M = E} is consistent; the open implication is whether easiness always entails simple easiness.

evidence.quote: Statement. Does easiness imply simple easiness? According to [Jacopini, 1975] a closed term E is easy if, for any other closed term M, the theory λβ + {M = E} is consistent. Clearly each simple easy term is easy, but the vice versa is open.

accepted.question_text: Find a type assignment system in which exactly the hereditary permutations are assigned types of one fixed shape. A closed lambda-term M is a hereditary permutation when its Böhm tree has no ⊥ label, every variable occurs exactly once, the head variable is the first abstracted variable, and all other variables occur one level below their abstractions.

evidence.quote: Statement. Type theoretic characterisation of hereditary permutations
The problem is to find a type assignment system in which all and only the hereditary permutations get types of a fixed shape.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether higher-order matching remains decidable when types are built from many atomic type variables rather than a single atom. This includes the special-case retraction problem of deciding whether ρ ◁ τ holds for given types ρ and τ in the many-atoms setting.

evidence.quote: Statement. Is higher-order matching decidable with many atoms? It has recently been proved [Stirling, 2009] that the higher-order matching problem is decidable. However, the proof method only applies to the “classical” case of the problem: when all types are built from a single atom. Therefore, the problem remains open for the generalized case of types built from an arbitrary number of type variables.
The problem to decide if ρ ◁ τ holds for given ρ and τ is decidable for a single atom but for many atoms it remains an open question.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists a continuously complete CPO model of lambda-calculus whose theory is exactly λβη or exactly λβ. Equivalently, decide whether λβ or λβη are precisely the equations that hold in all extensional continuously complete CPO models, or whether some filter model has exactly one of those theories.
accepted.context_brief: continuously complete CPO models for λβ or λβη

evidence.quote: Statement. Is there a continuously complete CPO model of the λ-calculus whose theory is precisely λβη or λβ?

The problem can be phrased equivalently as: • Is λβ (or λβη) the only equations which hold in all (extensional) continuously complete CPO models of λ-calculus? • Is there a filter model whose theory is precisely λβη or λβ?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether Expansion Postponement holds for every pure type system: namely, whether every derivable judgement has a derivation in which the expansion rule is used at most once and only as the final step.

evidence.quote: Statement. Does Expansion Postponement hold for every PTS?
Expansion Postponement (EP) is the conjecture that every derivable judgement in a PTS has a derivation in which the expansion rule is used at most once, as the final step in the derivation.

accepted.question_text: Understand what solving equations of the form M X = N X for arbitrary normal forms M and N can be reduced to or inferred from by passing to the associated deed equation D_M X = D_N X under the injective mapping from normal forms to deeds.

evidence.quote: Statement. On the equational meaning of deeds
The question is as follows: What can we understand about the solution of the equation M X = N X, where M, N are arbitrary normal forms, by looking at the equation D_M X = D_N X?

accepted.question_text: Determine how many fixed points a combinator, meaning a closed lambda term, can have in λβ-calculus. In particular, characterize the possible cardinalities of the set of its fixed points beyond the known result that having one normal-form fixed point forces either infinitely many fixed points or exactly one.
accepted.context_brief: number of fixed points of a combinator

evidence.quote: Statement. How many fixed points can a combinator have? The question is how many fixed points can a combinator (i.e. a closed term) have in the λβ-calculus.

accepted.question_text: Construct an easy assignment of ordinals, possibly transfinite, to terms of the simply typed lambda calculus such that whenever a term M β-reduces to N, the assigned ordinal strictly decreases. The point of the problem is to obtain a direct, easy proof of strong normalization from such an ordinal assignment rather than one that presupposes strong normalization.
accepted.context_brief: easy ordinal assignment for simply typed lambda calculus

evidence.quote: Statement. Assign (in an ‘easy’ way) ordinals to terms of the simply typed lambda calculus such that reduction of the term yields a smaller ordinal.

Construct an ‘easy’ assignment of (possibly trans-finite) ordinals to terms of the simply typed lambda calculus, i.e. a map # : Λ→ → { α | α is an ordinal }, such that ∀M, N ∈ Λ→ [ M →β N ⇒ #M > #N ].
But the purpose of this ‘koan’ is to prove SN in an easy way and this ‘solution’ presupposes that SN holds.
